newsitem.title: CANADA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON STILL FAVORED BUT BETTORS PLAYING BAILEY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON STILL FAVORED BUT BETTORS PLAYING BAILEY.

text.p: Michael Johnson is the early favourite for his world's fastest man showdown with Donovan Bailey, but the early money is being bet on the Canadian, the Canadian Press news agency reported on Wednesday.
Sports books in Las Vegas say there is not much money being bet yet on the 150-meter SkyDome match race on June 1 between the world's two best sprinters.

At the Stardust Hotel, bettors have to put up $2 to win $1 back if Johnson, the American 200-meter world record-holder wins. Bailey backers put up $1 to get a $2 return if the 100-meter world record-holder triumphs.
"It was more of a novelty at first," Bob Scucci, a shift manager in the Stardust's race and sports book, told the news agency.

"We had a lot of lookers and not a lot of people wagering. But lately it's picked up and most of the money is going on Bailey. But mostly it's what we call small money and small money generally goes on the side with the bigger return."
Johnson is only a slight favourite at the Mirage. There, bettors put down $2.10 to win $1 on Johnson; $1.70 on Bailey to win $1.
The betting line is established to create equal betting interest on either athlete, guaranteeing a financial win for the house.
